clue.text: Sprawled out in moorland barn and in On The Waterfront

indicators.note: something sprawled out lies jumbled and loose, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone lies sprawled in a moorland barn, and the clue tacks on a waterfront setting.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a description rather than a synonym: the answer is the actor who starred in On The Waterfront (1954).
explanation.definitionFit: The actor won the Best Actor Oscar for playing Terry Malloy in the 1954 film On The Waterfront.

clue.text: Took advantage of a leading veteran who was ill

indicators.note: leading means the front letter of the word veteran is taken

parts.note: to be ill is to have ailed

explanation.surface: Someone exploited an old soldier who happened to be sick.
explanation.definitionFit: To avail oneself of something is to make use of it, a synonym of taking advantage.

clue.text: Having connections to Kindle novel

indicators.note: novel as an adjective means new or reworked, so the letters of Kindle are arranged afresh

explanation.surface: Something has links to the Kindle, Amazon's e-reader, where you might read a novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' suggests a book read on a Kindle, but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Being joined or associated with something is a synonym for having connections with it.

clue.text: Fate's no choice of letters

definitions.meaning: in Norse myth the three Fates are the weird sisters who spin destiny
the letters ... offer a choice between a letter and itself, which is no choice at all

explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as N-OR-N: a choice of letters which is no real choice, both options being the same letter.
explanation.definitionFit: In Norse mythology this is one of the three goddesses of destiny, the equivalent of the Greek Fates.

clue.text: Blushing left-winger was impertinent

parts.note: a red is a socialist or communist, someone on the political left
to cheek someone is to be impertinent, so was impertinent gives cheeked

explanation.surface: A socialist flushed after being rude to someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone blushing has a face flushed pink with embarrassment, a synonym.

clue.text: Genuine vindication somewhat upset Pink Panther star

indicators.note: upset says the hidden letters are read backwards
somewhat says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A real vindication seems to have unsettled a film star.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'upset' turns the hidden run NEVIN, taken from 'Genuine vindication', upside down.
explanation.definitionFit: David Niven played the jewel thief Sir Charles Lytton in the original 1963 film The Pink Panther.

clue.text: Growth of very large steel nuts

parts.note: OS is the clothing abbreviation for outsize, meaning very large

indicators.note: nuts means crazy or deranged, so the letters of steel are scrambled

explanation.surface: Something grows from a pile of big steel nuts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nuts' looks like hardware made of steel but is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a vet's term for a bony lump that grows on a horse's leg, an example of a growth.

clue.text: Brother panned, playing in Tinker, Tailor, Soldier, Spy

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters are messing about and rearranging themselves

explanation.surface: A sibling was slated by the critics while acting in the le Carré drama.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing in' reads as acting in the drama, but 'playing' is the anagram signal and 'in Tinker, Tailor, Soldier, Spy' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: This English actor played Toby Esterhase in the 1979 BBC television serial of le Carré's spy novel.

clue.text: Reminding Garbo, losing nothing, involved as Anastasia

indicators.note: involved means tangled or intricate, so the letters are mixed up
losing says a piece is dropped from the name Garbo

parts.note: nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone's performance as Anastasia recalls Greta Garbo, though lacking something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing nothing' takes O out of GARBO to leave GARB; 'involved' then rearranges REMINDING with GARB.
explanation.definitionFit: The Swedish actress won an Oscar for playing the title role in the 1956 film Anastasia.

clue.text: Lou Grant endears cast

indicators.note: cast as in thrown about or recast, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Casting a likeable actor made the character Lou Grant popular.
explanation.definitionFit: The American actor played newsman Lou Grant in The Mary Tyler Moore Show and in his own spin-off series.

clue.text: Dr Who cars into the river

indicators.note: into means one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: the Don is a river in Yorkshire and in Russia
Avis is a car-rental company

explanation.surface: The Doctor drives cars into a river.
explanation.definitionFit: Peter Davison played the fifth Doctor in the BBC science-fiction series Doctor Who.

clue.text: Reputation embraces leading light of Hulk

indicators.note: embraces means the first piece holds the second within it

parts.note: note in the sense of distinction or renown, as in a person of note

indicators.note: leading means the front letter of the word light is taken

explanation.surface: A green giant's fame includes his being a guiding star.
explanation.definitionFit: Nick Nolte played David Banner, the scientist father of the title character, in Ang Lee's 2003 film Hulk.

clue.text: Perry in Friends as thriller writer

definitions.meaning: the role Matthew Perry played in the US sitcom Friends
Raymond, the American author of hard-boiled detective novels featuring Philip Marlowe

explanation.surface: An actor from a sitcom is recast as a crime novelist.
explanation.definitionFit: The surname belongs both to Matthew Perry's sitcom role and to the creator of private eye Philip Marlowe.

clue.text: Emile is now recast as French philosopher and mystic

indicators.note: recast means formed again in a new shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man called Emile is now being presented as a French thinker.
explanation.definitionFit: Simone Weil (1909-1943) was a French philosopher, political activist and Christian mystic.

clue.text: Poles starting trek to mountain in the heat of the night!

definitions.text: in the heat of the night!

parts.note: rods are long poles

indicators.note: starting means the opening letter of the word trek

parts.note: the Eiger is a famous Swiss mountain

explanation.surface: Climbers with poles begin trekking up a mountain in the night's heat.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the 1967 film title In the Heat of the Night, disguised as a description of the climb.
explanation.definitionFit: Rod Steiger won the Best Actor Oscar for playing police chief Gillespie in the film In the Heat of the Night.

clue.text: Unfinished detailed examination of breeding establishment

indicators.note: unfinished says the final letter is cut off

parts.note: a study is a detailed examination of a subject

explanation.surface: An incomplete survey of a horse farm.
explanation.definitionFit: A stud is a farm where horses are kept for breeding.

clue.text: Could be Hank or Chuck — a chap embracing another

indicators.note: embracing means the first piece holds the second within it

parts.note: a chap is a man
another chap, here a man's name, Eric

explanation.surface: Two men with nicknames, one hugging another fellow.
explanation.walkthrough: Hank and Chuck are typical US forms of Henry and Charles, so the definition is by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Hank and Chuck are typical names of men from the United States, so each is an example of a national.

clue.text: Keep quiet — it's semi- confidential

indicators.note: semi- means half, so only the first half of the word is kept

parts.note: ...-... means secret or confidential

explanation.surface: Someone is told to say nothing because the matter is partly secret.
explanation.definitionFit: To shush someone, or fall silent, is a synonym of keeping quiet.

clue.text: Pastor, say, who pictured Piglet and Sam

indicators.note: say means the word is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: a pastor is a shepherd of his flock

explanation.surface: A clergyman is asked who drew the Winnie-the-Pooh characters.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition covers two people: E.H. Shepard, who illustrated Piglet in the Pooh books, and Sam Shepard, the American playwright and actor.
explanation.definitionFit: E.H. Shepard drew the Pooh illustrations and Sam Shepard was a US dramatist, so the surname fits both.

clue.text: Understood Heath E. was saintly

parts.note: roger is radio talk for message received and understood
a moor is open heathland
the letter E, set out as an initial

explanation.surface: A man named Heath E. was virtuous, or so we gather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heath E.' looks like a person's name with an initial; the definition refers to the TV series The Saint, in which this actor played Simon Templar.
explanation.definitionFit: Roger Moore starred as Simon Templar, known as the Saint, in the 1960s ITV series.

clue.text: Opening gold reserve, holding one key

indicators.note: holding means the first pieces contain the next ones

parts.note: or is gold in heraldry
ice means cold reserve or aloofness
one is the Roman numeral I
F is a musical key

explanation.surface: A bank opens its gold reserve, which holds a single key.
explanation.definitionFit: An orifice is a hole or mouth, a synonym of an opening.

clue.text: A Witch of Eastwick or one from St Andrews, say

indicators.note: say means the word is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: St Andrews is in Fife, a Scottish county, so someone from there is a Fifer

explanation.surface: A witch from a film is compared to a Scot from a golfing town.
explanation.walkthrough: Fife is a region in eastern Scotland; St Andrews, home of golf, lies within it.
explanation.definitionFit: Michelle Pfeiffer played one of the three witches in the 1987 film The Witches of Eastwick.

clue.text: Robin Hood, fashionable outside of Northampton

parts.note: fly is slang for smart or stylish

indicators.note: outside of means the end letters of the word Northampton

explanation.surface: An outlaw is stylishly dressed on the edge of a Midlands town.
explanation.definitionFit: Errol Flynn played the title role in the 1938 film The Adventures of Robin Hood.

clue.text: Contrite, I step outside

indicators.note: outside means the piece for step goes around the letter I

parts.note: a rung is a step on a ladder

explanation.surface: Someone sorry steps outside in shame.
explanation.definitionFit: Being remorseful and regretting something, the sense in which the answer and contrite are linked.

clue.text: Has snow melted?

indicators.note: melted snow has lost its form, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A simple question about whether the snow has thawed.
explanation.definitionFit: To possess something is to have it, so the two verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: All resembling Gothic maybe

definitions.meaning: things all resembling one another are all of the same kind
Gothic is a typeface, so read the phrase as belonging to a type

explanation.walkthrough: Gothic is a family of typefaces, so a Gothic font is one of a type; the first definition is the ordinary sense of similar things.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means of the same kind, and a Gothic font belongs to a typeface.

clue.text: Whence a lineman involved with CIA

indicators.note: involved means tangled together, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A telephone lineman's home town is mixed up with US intelligence.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition alludes to the Glen Campbell song Wichita Lineman.
explanation.definitionFit: The song Wichita Lineman places its telephone engineer in this Kansas city, so it is where he comes from.

clue.text: Dennis old and dissolute, starred in Two's Company and Never the Twain

definitions.text: starred in Two's Company and Never the Twain

indicators.note: dissolute suggests loose living, so the letters are let loose and rearranged

explanation.surface: An elderly, debauched Dennis turns out to be a sitcom actor.
explanation.definitionFit: Donald Sinden was the British actor who starred in both of these ITV sitcoms of the 1970s and 80s.
